title: Coherent projection comparison presentations for cospans
statement:
Use simplicial sets, quasicategories, right-pinched mapping spaces, coherent cones, and weak equivalences as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the canonical pinch maps of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison], and the coherent cone calculus of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Fix a quasicategory $E$, a cospan $F:J=\Lambda^2_2\to E$ and a test vertex $x$. Write $a=F(0)$, $b=F(1)$, $c=F(2)$. For any diagram $G:K\to E$, put $R_G(x)=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)}(\Delta_Kx,G)$. Restriction and evaluation on these spaces are induced by the actual restriction and evaluation functors. Let $R_L(x),R_R(x)$ be the restrictions of $R_F(x)$ to the edges $0\to2$ and $1\to2$, with initial evaluations $e_L:R_L(x)\to\operatorname{Map}_E(x,a)$ and $e_R:R_R(x)\to\operatorname{Map}_E(x,b)$ and final evaluations $q_L,q_R$ into $\operatorname{Map}_E(x,c)$.

A coherent pullback comparison presentation consists of sections $s_L,s_R$ of $e_L,e_R$, homotopies $h_L:s_L\circ e_L\simeq1_{R_L(x)}$ and $h_R:s_R\circ e_R\simeq1_{R_R(x)}$, and a simplicial map
$$j:R_F(x)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_E(x,a)\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}_E(x,c)}\operatorname{Map}_E(x,b).$$
The two maps to the base are $q_L\circ s_L$ and $q_R\circ s_R$, representatives of composition with the actual cospan legs. For maps $f:A\to C$, $g:B\to C$, the path model used here is $A\times_{C,\mathrm{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,C)\times_{\mathrm{ev}_1,C}B$, retaining all higher simplices. The projections of $j$ are exactly evaluation at vertices $0,1$. Its path is required to fit in a simplicial family of triangles in $\operatorname{Map}_E(x,c)$: edge $01$ is that output path, edge $12$ is the restriction of $q_Rh_R$, and edge $02$ is the restriction of $q_Lh_L$. Thus the third vertex is the actual common component at $c$ of the original coherent cone. This triangle, the endpoint projections, and the section homotopies are part of the presentation, not arbitrary maps satisfying only weak-equivalence conditions.

For a supplied coherent cone $\mu$ on $G$ with apex $p$, a map $L:\operatorname{Map}_E(x,p)\to R_G(x)$ represents composition with $\mu$ when, after the canonical pinch to unpinched arrows, a family of triangles has consecutive edges the constant-diagram image of the incoming arrow and the actual coherent transformation of $\mu$, and long edge endpoint-preservingly homotopic to the pinch of $L$. Define the mapping-space test for a family of presentations $P(F,x)$ to mean: such representatives $L$ exist for every supplied cone and test vertex; a cone is limiting exactly when every such $j\circ L$ is a weak equivalence for every $x$; and for a morphism of cones, postcomposition with its actual apex arrow makes the comparisons commute up to simplicial homotopy. Postcomposition with that apex arrow has the same triangle-and-endpoint characterization.

A transformation between cones on possibly different cospans is an edge in $E\times\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\operatorname{Fun}(J,E))$ with the supplied cone endpoints, whose source endpoint in $\operatorname{Fun}(J,E)$ is the constant-diagram image of its apex edge. Its other endpoint is the specified diagram transformation. Define naturality for changing diagrams to mean that postcomposition representatives $a$ on apex mapping spaces and $b$ on the coherent-cone spaces, characterized by their actual edges and the same triangle equations, induce a path-model map $t$ with homotopies $t\circ j_F\simeq j_G\circ b$ and $t\circ j_F\circ L_F\simeq j_G\circ L_G\circ a$. Finally, define equivalence invariance to mean that a simplicial interval family of cone arrows, with both endpoint equations imposed in every degree and with equivalence edges on its apex and diagram coordinates, has a limiting source cone exactly when its target cone is limiting. These are definitions of the comparison data and its tests; no existence or universal-property assertion is made here.
